messages:
maya: Heads-up — FP8 bakeoff on the 13B model surfaced a reproducible drop on a small subset of multi-turn reasoning/math prompts (~0.9% BLEU / noticeable token churn). Repro steps below. @tony fyi for routing impact :eyes:
tonny: can you paste the traffic split you suggested last week?
maya: repro: run local eval harness on the 'arith-multi' golden set with seed=42, ctx=2048. Command:
```
python eval.py --model ./runs/13b-fp8 --suite arith-multi --seed 42 --ctx 2048 --compare ../runs/13b-awq
```
Output note: divergences start ~step 4 of multistep chains, often hallucinate extra constraint-solving steps. sample diff attached (short).
devon: thanks — do we have a kernel-level cause? FP8 rounding vs attention kv-cache?
maya: initial profiler points at accumulator saturation in matmul for long prefixes; differences amplify in subsequent tokens. Not a memory corruption, more numerical drift.
quant-bot: [anomaly] FP8-run-200123: BLEU_drop=0.91%, avg_token_entropy_delta=0.07, drift_detected=true
jenna: operational ask: what's the rollout plan? need guidance for hosted/dedicated/private.
maya: proposal: 1) Hosted: hold FP8 at 0% for public traffic until we validate safety-gates; run shadow 10% of traffic for 48h with auto-eval on golden sets. 2) Dedicated: allow 5% canary on committed pools with strict timeout and rollback hook. 3) Private: opt-in only, require customer signoff and provide explicit quant-profile notes.
tonny: suggest more nuanced routing: prefer AWQ for buckets with high-cost prompts (>=2.5s baseline) and keep FP8 for short-chat micro workloads. Also set fallback priority list: AWQ -> GPTQ -> FP8 (i.e., if variance exceeds threshold fall back up the stack).
maya: fallback rules I suggest: - metric triggers: BLEU_drop > 0.5% OR avg_token_entropy_delta > 0.03 OR regression_on_golden>fail_count(5) - action: immediate per-route split cut from X%->0 and route to AWQ variant; annotate trace and create rollback PR.
devon: can we automate prefix-detection so risky long-reasoning contexts get AWQ by default?\moya: (typo) maya: yes, we can use prefix heuristics: if user prompt matches /\b(math|solve|prove|argue)\b/ and tokens>128 -> force AWQ. Put rules in policy engine.
jenna: SLA implications? Dedicated customers expect consistent latencies.
tonny: for Dedicated, accept slightly higher cost: prefer deterministic variants (AWQ/GPTQ) in the hot path; FP8 relegated to burst-only or background jobs.
maya: experiment next steps: 1) run 48h shadow traffic with golden-set perf and in-prod logging, 2) collect auto-evals every 2h, 3) if any trigger fires, auto-roll to AWQ and alert #eng-oncall + the customer ext if private.
devon: add smoke tests to CI matching the arith-multi set to catch regressions on merges. Also add a per-commit numeric tolerance gating.
jenna: ok. I'll draft runbook blurb for SLO docs and incident triggers.
maya: thanks — i'll open the experiment PR with configs. tagging @devon @tony to review the policy YAMLs once up. :thumbsup:
quant-bot: [action] experiment 200123_FP8_shadow created, monitor=arith-multi, eval_interval=2h, fallback=AWQ
tonny: small nit — spell my name right it's tony :grimacing:
maya: fixed. will push PR in ~20m.
